findings.title: `pipeline.background_idle_timeout_s` accepts zero or negative values
findings.description: The key is a plain `int` with no range check. `set_config` has no validator hook, and `_coerce_value` only runs `int(raw_value)`. A value of `0` or a negative number reaches `asyncio.timeout(idle_s)` in `SDKExecutionSession._read_turn`. The timer then fires immediately once a background agent is running. `_stop_background` kills every agent and `dispatch` returns partial text. The user gets no sign of a bad setting, only agents killed at once. The project's fail-fast rule says to catch this where the value is set or read. Reject values `<= 0` in `_background_idle_timeout_s` (or add a per-key validator) and raise `ValueError`.

findings.title: `TimeoutError` catch in `_collect_turns` can mistake a foreign timeout for an idle timeout
findings.description: `except TimeoutError` wraps all of `_read_turn_with_retry`, not only the `asyncio.timeout(idle_s)` block in `_read_turn`. `_read_turn_with_retry` also covers the retry `asyncio.sleep` and the SDK iteration. If anything inside raises a `TimeoutError` of its own, it is handled as "background agents idle". The agents are stopped and the dispatch returns partial text as if it succeeded, with a misleading warning. Narrow the handler. For example, have `_read_turn` convert its own timeout into a dedicated `IdleTimeout` exception and catch that. A bare `TimeoutError` can then still propagate as a real failure.

findings.title: Config reads inside the session and dispatch hot path (dependency inversion)
findings.description: `SDKExecutionSession._background_idle_timeout_s` and `open_pipeline_session` call `get_typed_config` directly. `one_shot_dispatch_with_telemetry` in `pipeline/actions/dispatch.py` does the same. These are low-level classes and functions that reach into the global config store, so their tests must `patch(f"{_MOD}.get_typed_config", ...)`. The review rules treat that kind of monkeypatching as a sign of inverted dependencies. The timeout reads from `base_options.cwd or Path.cwd()` on every dispatch with a waiting agent. Resolve the three pipeline settings once at the composition root (executor or `open_pipeline_session`). Pass them into the session as constructor fields, for example `idle_timeout_s`. Pass `auto_memory` and `user_settings` into `one_shot_dispatch_with_telemetry` the same way. This also lets one place validate the timeout value.

findings.title: `sdk_session.py` has grown large and mixes responsibilities
findings.description: The diff adds turn collection, rate-limit retry, idle timeout, background-agent stop, an unusable-session state, seeding and settings policy to `SDKExecutionSession`. Moving the pure bookkeeping into `sdk_turns.py` was the right call. The stream-reading loop (`_collect_turns`, `_read_turn_with_retry`, `_read_turn`, `_stop_background`, about 100 lines) still lives in the session class. It is also hard to follow: `_collect_turns` has five exit paths and mutates `turns` flags (`own_result_seen`, `waiting_logged`, `progressed`) from outside. That is Law of Demeter pressure and works against the project's roughly 300-line file guideline. Consider moving the read loop into `DispatchTurns` or a small collaborator that takes the stream as input.

findings.title: Behavior change for `sq serve` agents: auto-memory is now always forced off
findings.description: `create_agent` now always sets `kwargs["env"]` through `sdk_settings_options`. `AgentConfig.auto_memory` defaults to `False`, so every SDK agent that does not opt in, including `setting_sources=None` callers like `sq serve`, now gets `CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY=1`. Before, only `setting_sources == []` did. The inline comment and slice D11 state this is deliberate. Make sure the release notes mention it, because `sq serve` users lose auto-memory silently.

findings.title: Static-typing escapes added
findings.description: `setting_sources=settings["setting_sources"],  # pyright: ignore[reportArgumentType]` and `base_env=kwargs.get("env"),  # type: ignore[arg-type]` suppress type errors instead of fixing them. `SdkSettings` already types `setting_sources` as `list[str]`, so the pyright ignore may point at an SDK literal-type mismatch. A `cast` to the SDK's `SettingSource` list, or a typed `kwargs` accumulator, would remove both ignores. Several test helpers (`scripted_session`, `sdk_text`, etc.) also return `object`, which forces many `# type: ignore[attr-defined]` comments in the tests. Typing the helpers would remove them.

findings.title: Docstring reference to a table that sits in a comment
findings.description: `SystemPromptMode`'s docstring says "the four rows of the table above". That table is a code comment inside `AgentConfig` (lines 54-58), not directly above the enum. Point the docstring at `AgentConfig.use_default_system_prompt`.

findings.title: Test coverage for the new behavior
findings.description:
New behavior has tests alongside the implementation:
- Bool coercion, with parametrized spellings and an invalid-value path.
- The background ledger.
- Waiting for agents and joining the follow-up turn.
- The idle timeout, including `stop_task` failure, and the no-timer foreground case.
- Dropping a leftover injected turn.
- Subagent prose exclusion.
- Unusable-session after a failed reconnect.
- A per-path settings-policy matrix.
- Seed-framing exactly once.
- Resume seeding of a lazily connected session.

The failure modes are observable: ERROR and WARNING log assertions are present. A load test for the new waiting and timeout paths is absent. The rules ask for one on concurrency paths, but the timer is exercised with short real sleeps.

findings.title: Exception handling follows project policy
findings.description: The broad `except Exception` in `_stop_background` carries `# noqa: BLE001`, a justification (the SDK raises a bare `Exception`) and `logger.exception`. `_reconnect` records `unusable_reason`, logs at ERROR and re-raises. `config_set` now also catches `ValueError`, so a bad bool exits with code 1 and a message.
